note: Oilers Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru of HI-67 (Moji to Singapore via Manila), both minor damage; both reached Manila. BANG's sheets claimed 2(a) a large engine-aft freighter or tanker sunk (fits Sarawak Maru, hit in the bow), 2(b) a large passenger freighter sunk with a hole under the bridge (fits Miri Maru, hit under the bridge), and 2(c) a freighter probably sunk (no Japanese record of a third ship hit). FRUPAC relayed the claim as 2 AK sunk, 1 AK probably sunk

japanese.original: 二九日 一五一五 N一七-一三 E一一八-二二 みりい丸 さらわく丸 (小破)
japanese.translation: 29th, 1515, N 17°13′ E 118°22′: Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru (minor damage)

note: The destroyer Kuri reported being under torpedo attack with no damage at 0515 I, nine minutes after BANG fired (0506 I), at a position about 17 nm from BANG's. SEAHORSE had attacked the same convoy four hours earlier (0054 I) and was not firing then. BANG's sheet claimed damage to 1 AK; the Japanese record has no ship hit at this time

japanese.original: 〃 〇五一五 N一九-二二 E一一五-四三 栗 我雷撃ヲ受ク被害ナシ 制圧中(?)
japanese.translation: (4th) 0515, N 19°22′ E 115°43′, from Kuri: we are under torpedo attack, no damage; suppressing (the last word probably 制圧中)
